newsitem.title: SENEGAL: Senegal to re-run local elections in 100 centres.
newsitem.headline: Senegal to re-run local elections in 100 centres.

text.p: Senegal authorities have ordered a rerun of chaotic local elections in 100 polling centres in the capital where many people were unable to vote.
Voting on Sunday was extended to midnight after delays and poor organisation. Some polling stations had not even opened at the official close of polls at 6 p.m. (1800 GMT).

"For the centres that did not have sufficient time, it has been decided that voting should be postponed to a date that we will announce later," Interior Minister Abdourahmane Sow told reporters on Sunday night.
He said the logistics problems were due to the fact that it was the first time Senegal was holding muncipal, ward and regional elections at the same time.

Correspondents for private radio stations reported scences of confusion in the interior similar to that in Dakar, where voters complained of a shortage of everything from voter lists and cards to polling officials.
The opposition denounced the confusion, saying it was a ploy by the government to rig the vote.

"As a Senegalese I'm ashamed that at the dawn of the 21st century, we are unable to organise elections," said chief opposition leader Abdoulaye Wade, who is also a minister in President Abdou Diouf's Socialist Party-led government.
"It is deliberate so that under the cover of darkness the Socialist Party will rig the ballots," he said.

The elections in Dakar were seen as a test of popularity between Wade and Diouf, whose Socialist Party is trying to recapture the urban vote it lost to the opposition in presidential and parliamentary polls in 1993.
Wade hopes to emerge as mayor of Dakar.
Just over three million voters were to cast their ballots, with 14 parties competing for for 826 regional council seats, 421 municipal council seats, 3,559 district seats and 15,386 rural seats.
